requirements.statement: Managed application logging must use the injected kernel logger or a child of that logger. A concrete logger must be constructed only in its declared adapter or composition root.
requirements.when: The application uses dcouplr-managed components and logging. Pure value construction and a declared logger adapter are valid exceptions.
requirements.verify: Assert the real construction and call graph, configured logger replacement, and child propagation. Add a failing control that creates or imports an unrelated logger in a managed component.
canaries: kernel logging delegates to the configured adapter
logger gate child keeps its configured adapter

requirements.statement: A scoped logger must preserve its parent and sibling contexts. The application must verify the intended binding precedence and must not assume that a child logger deep-copies nested data.
requirements.when: The application uses child loggers for request, organization, correlation, or other shared bindings.
requirements.verify: Assert parent, sibling, child and call-local contexts through the actual configured adapter. Verify that context ownership prevents cross-request mutation and that sensitive data is removed before logging. Include a wrong-scope failing control.
canaries: default logger child bindings preserve parent and sibling contexts
default logger call context overrides child and parent bindings
default logger child bindings are shallow values

requirements.statement: The configured logger must enforce its level policy on writes. A caller must check isLevelEnabled before it constructs expensive optional logging data. The caller must not assume that the gate prevents adapter calls for a disabled level.
requirements.when: The logger has disabled levels or a caller constructs costly optional context or messages.
requirements.verify: Assert actual enabled and disabled writes for the configured adapter and confirm that a disabled expensive context builder is not called. Include a non-filtering adapter and an eager-context failing control.
canaries: default logger info threshold filters all six levels
disabled logging still calls the configured adapter
level guard prevents expensive context construction
eager disabled logging still constructs its context

requirements.statement: A caller must use the public logging overload that preserves its intended message, error, structured context and source attribution. A fatal log must not replace the actual throw, rejection, return or shutdown required by the application.
requirements.when: The application uses context-first, source-instance or Error-first overloads, or relies on failure control flow.
requirements.verify: Assert actual adapter arguments and caller control flow, including an Error with a message override. Keep attribution separate from identity or authorization. Include a fatal-only failing control when termination is required.
canaries: logger gate normalizes context and source overloads
logger gate preserves Error-first adapter arguments
default logger error context permits an explicit err override
fatal logging returns normally and execution continues

requirements.statement: A buffered logger must have an owned flush and failure policy. A shutdown or checkpoint that requires completed logging must await the actual flush. A synchronous unbuffered logger may omit flush.
requirements.when: The application buffers logging data or requires logging completion before it ends an operation or process.
requirements.verify: Hold the configured adapter flush with a deferred promise and assert that the actual shutdown waits. Verify rejection handling and the unbuffered no-flush case. Include a missing-await failing control. A resolved flush does not prove remote retention unless the adapter contract says so.
canaries: logger gate waits for an adapter flush promise
logger gate propagates a rejected flush
logger gate permits a synchronous adapter without flush

requirements.statement: An application must not treat a logger monitor event as proof of sink delivery, complete child bindings, serialized error data or authorization. Required audit evidence must come from an explicit tested contract.
requirements.when: The application consumes logging monitor events, inspector output or logs as audit evidence.
requirements.verify: Assert sink records and monitor payloads separately through the actual adapters, including child bindings, Error-first calls and disabled levels. Verify the required audit fields and retention at their owning boundary. Include a monitor-only failing control.
canaries: logger monitor does not include adapter child bindings
logger monitor Error-first context is not serialized error evidence
disabled logging still calls the configured adapter
